text:
anya: Quick check — oak-pp1 (onprem) is showing ~15% higher p95 tail latency compared to hosted for gen requests (seq=32). Can someone help validate parity and narrow down root cause? I ran the same model binary and weights. Suspects: NIC MTU, irqbalance, hugepages, or block-device scheduler.

nate: I can run a quick micro-benchmark. Which workload config? same batch/seq? also do you want raw throughput or latency distribution + flamegraphs?

anya: thanks @nate. Use the gen-32 profile from bench-run-2026-03 (batch=1, warmup=200, iters=1000). We care about tail latency and kernel/User stacks. Flamegraphs would be ideal.

infra-bot: perf-job queued: job-1774509876-01 on oak-pp1 (node=o1-rack3). ETA ~10m. Logs: https://internal.logs/redwood/perf/job-1774509876-01

kevin: FYI oak-pp1 is on 5.15 kernel, NIC firmware v2.4.0, MTU=1500, irqbalance=enabled. Hosted baseline uses MTU=9000 and irqbalance disabled for dedicated racks. That could explain packetization and softirq differences.

nate: running wrk-style latency probe + perf record. Command I'll use:

```
# warmup
./bench --model my-model --profile gen-32 --warmup 200 --iters 1000 
# latency probe
wrk -t8 -c256 -d30s http://oak-pp1:8080/generate
# perf capture
sudo perf record -F 99 -g -- sleep 30
sudo perf script > out.perf
# flamegraph
git clone https://github.com/brendangregg/FlameGraph.git && ./FlameGraph/stackcollapse-perf.pl out.perf | ./FlameGraph/flamegraph.pl > perf-flame.svg
```

sarah: also collect `dmesg -T`, `ethtool -S eth0`, `cat /sys/devices/system/cpu/online`, and `cat /proc/interrupts` — I want to check CPU isolation and irq distribution. If possible, snapshot cgroup config: `cat /sys/fs/cgroup/*/cpuset.cpus` on both nodes.

kevin: note: oak-pp1 has transparent hugepages=always. Hosted baseline uses thp=never. That influences mmap/allocator behavior for the runtime. If you can toggle and re-run quick perf that'd be useful.

nate: started capture. Will post the flamegraph and perf tarball here when done. If we see irq softirq hotspots around eth driver, we can try MTU 9000 on a single node to test impact.

anya: perfect. Can we also get a run with `GOMP_CPU_AFFINITY` pinned like hosted (we typically pin to 0-31) — that was overlooked on oak-pp1.

nate: good call. I'll do two runs: default and cpuset pinned. tagging @kevin for kernel/hugepage toggle help.

kevin: I can toggle thp and MTU on a maintenance window. If you need immediate, I can flip MTU to 9000 on o1-rack3-02 temporarily (may require switch config). Ping me before you start the second run.

sarah: add to checklist: record driver RX/TX rings, RSS queue distribution (`ethtool -n eth0`), and `numastat -c` to ensure NUMA allocation matches GPU locality (if GPUs are involved).

nate: upload: https://internal.artifacts/redwood/perf/job-1774509876-01/trace.tar.gz — contains perf.data, out.perf, flamegraph.svg, dmesg, ethtool outputs. Initial take: top of flamegraph shows user-space stacks (runtime hot loop) but there's a noticeable softirq spike on CPU 12.

anya: thanks. @kevin can you try MTU 9000 on that node during maintenance and tell us when it's done so nate can re-run? Also let's make an action: replicate hosted kernel boot flags (irqbalance=off, thp=never, cpuset pin) and re-run to measure delta.

kevin: I can schedule now. I'll update when MTU + thp toggled. ETA 30m.

infra-bot: job completed: job-1774509876-01 -> artifacts available at https://internal.artifacts/redwood/perf/job-1774509876-01/trace.tar.gz

anya: excellent. Once we have post-change numbers, we'll decide if this needs an infra-side baseline document for Private deployments (kernel + NIC recommended settings). If parity gap <=3% we'll call it good.

sarah: +1. If gap persists after kernel/NIC parity, we'll dig into allocator/numa/GPU driver versions next.

nate: will re-run after kevin flips MTU. Will post new perf tarball here.

anya: thanks team — appreciate the quick turnaround. :thumbsup:
